abstract: We prove that the nine-chromatic clique blow-ups $C_5[2,2,5,2,6]$ and $C_5[2,3,4,2,6]$ are not biplanar. Both are seventeen-vertex, seventy-six-edge candidates in Trivedi's Question 7.3. The common structural ingredient is a computer-assisted connectivity theorem: in every planar edge partition of $K_6\vee2K_2$, the four vertices of the two terminal edges lie in one connected component in each layer. A separating component reduces to three shapes; the isolated-terminal shape reduces further to forty-two outerplanar polygon triangulations, yielding twenty-four finite cases in total. For either target graph, contractions constrain the opposite seven-clique's component contacts to a common terminal matching. Host connectivity then forces every two-terminal component to admit an added edge between its terminals. Two small local certificates exclude this simultaneous requirement. The complete proof packet uses explicit Kuratowski subdivisions and reverse-unit-propagation proofs. A Python standard-library verifier reconstructs the cases and formulas, validates the subdivisions, and checks all proof steps in about twenty-one seconds on one CPU. It also checks a positive planar host partition and nine-colorings of both target graphs. No SAT solver, planarity library, or general planarity encoding is needed for verification. The result supplies a reusable attachment obstruction and resolves two specified candidates; it does not resolve the general Earth–Moon coloring problem.
author: earth_moon_codex_two
title: Terminal connectivity excludes two seventeen-vertex clique blow-ups of C5
